aria: Animated recap of the Warriors' 138 to 87 home win over New Orleans: Stephen Curry's three with 3:13 left in the third quarter, quarter-by-quarter scoring, his 25 points in 21 minutes, the top scorers, how the Warriors won, and the next game at Houston.
notes: Box score from the Warriors' 138–87 home win over the New Orleans Pelicans on Nov 9, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, checked against the Digest Sports box score, with game details from the AP (via Yahoo Sports), Field Level Media, NBC Sports Bay Area (via Yahoo Sports), Heavy and Yardbarker. All 138 Warriors points and all 87 Pelicans points are accounted for in both box scores, and the quarter scores add up to both totals and match the AP (35–20 after one, 72–43 at the half). The 51-point lead is the final margin (Covers, Yardbarker); New Orleans' only lead was 3–2 early in the first quarter (Covers, Digest Sports play-by-play). Bench points (60–41) are from NBC Sports Bay Area and match the box score; points in the paint and fast-break points are Covers'. Curry's 16 third-quarter points are from Field Level Media and the play-by-play; he did not play in the fourth (NBC Sports Bay Area says he sat for good in the third). Being the first team in NBA history to start 0–3 and then win eight straight is from Field Level Media and NBC Sports Bay Area. The next game is from Yardbarker and Heavy; the Rockets' record and the Warriors' standing are from the site's standings.

The play of the game is an original illustration of Stephen Curry's 22-foot three, assisted by Al Horford, with 3:13 left in the third quarter. Field Level Media says the Warriors led by 40, 101–61, at 3:13 of the third; the Digest Sports play-by-play shows that score came on Curry's three, from 98–61. It was the last of his 16 points in the quarter. The recaps don't describe how he got the shot, so it is drawn as a plain three. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Golden State Warriors or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Curry’s listed 6-foot-2 and 200 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with arms scaled to his reported 6-foot-4 wingspan (Sportskeeda), in the Warriors' home white with No. 30, with his approved look. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
